newsitem.title: MOROCCO: Morocco sells up to 62 pct of Sonasid.
newsitem.headline: Morocco sells up to 62 pct of Sonasid.

text.p: Morocco launched on Wednesday an international tender for sale of between 35 and 62 percent of steel giant Sonasid stock, as the second phase of the firm's privatisation, a Moroccan official said.

"The privatisation ministry engages the second phase of Sonasid privatisation by ceding a strategic participation of between 35 and 62 percent of its capital...The move aims to form a stable hard core of investors," an official at the privatisation ministry told Reuters.
The tender closes on February 28, 1997 at 1900 GMT, the ministry said.
Subscriptions should be sent to the Casablanca-based stockbroker Casablanca Finance Group CFG 25, it added.
Established in 1974 in the northern province of Nador, Societe Nationale de Siderurgie (Sonasid), has a capital of 390 million dirhams ($42.4 million).
Earlier this month, the firm's management announced it would build a new steel mill estimated at 738 million dirhams.
"The decision followed a feasability study carried out by British group W.S. Atkins in 1996," Ismail Douiri, analyst at Casablanca Finance Intermediation said.
The project will improve Sonasid continuing profitability and reinforce its global integration, Douiri added.
Douiri declined to give details on the expected local and foreign consortiums which are already interested in Morocco's steel giant.
Sonasid would supply 75 percent of the amount but did not say where the rest would be raised. The mill is expected to produce 616,000 tonnes of manufactured iron ore yearly.
Morocco offered 35 percent of the state-owned giant last year in a flotation worth 420 million dirhams. It was oversubscribed with demand totalling 675 million dirhams.
It manufactures concrete steel and wire rod, with average production of 420,000 tonnes satisfying more than 70 percent of domestic demand.
One of the 47 listed stocks on the Casablanca bourse, Sonasid was last traded at 375 dirhams.
